proposed.comparator_claim: Their delayed DAIPW estimator is consistent and asymptotically normal with consistently estimable variance under outcome--delay independence, moment and adaptive-weight conditions; Corollary 4.4 verifies these under a one-sided floor, prompt mass, and a polynomial finite-delay tail exponent of at least one half, with a nonzero-margin relaxation.

Adaptively weighted M-estimators yield asymptotically valid confidence regions for parameters under adaptive data collection, without addressing informative delayed revelation or fixed-horizon minimax expected length.
They construct time-uniform, nonparametric, nonasymptotic confidence sequences; that anytime-valid axis does not resolve informative terminal missingness or this fixed-horizon minimax-length problem.
The observed empirical mean is no longer an unbiased estimator of the expected reward.
They only assume that there is a bound on the tail of the delay.
With bounded or sub-Gaussian reward distributions, the upper bounds are optimal with a matching lower bound.
Maximum likelihood estimators from such a trial have the usual asymptotic properties.
The adaptively weighted estimator is consistent, and the studentized statistic is asymptotically normal.
Their stabilized estimator is asymptotically normal under consistent conditional-standard-deviation estimation.
They derive finite-sample optimal confidence intervals and sharp efficiency bounds under normal errors with known variance.
Their central limit theorem enables semiparametrically efficient inference at fixed sample sizes.
They derive the efficient influence function under propensities bounded away from zero and one.

prose_updates.tldr: Under the one-sided polynomial allocation condition \(\pi_t(1)\geq ct^{-\alpha}\), together with a control-arm floor, the measurable two-cohort gate-and-fallback interval has exact class-minimax expected-length order \(\max\{T^{-(1-\alpha)/2},(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}\}\) for the eventual arm-mean contrast. Shi, Wang, and Wu supply the design-side floor and delayed DAIPW asymptotics under an outcome--delay-independence model, whereas the present same-experiment hidden-tail converse permits informative delays; neither full class contains the other. The Liberali et al. discussion is a source audit and conditional prospective transfer, not a claim that their reported cardiovascular-trial percentile intervals equal this note's intervals.

project_justification.gap: Shi, Wang, and Wu prove delayed DAIPW consistency, asymptotic normality, and variance consistency under independent outcomes and delays, moment conditions, and adaptive-weight restrictions; they do not establish uniform honesty or minimax expected interval length. Delayed reward-dependent bandit work supplies regret lower bounds rather than a same-experiment interval-length frontier for an eventual causal contrast.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is the exact fixed-horizon expected-length frontier under a one-sided rare-arm exploration floor and a control floor when logged propensities may oscillate, within-arm revelation may be informative, and prespecified post-recruitment follow-up changes what is observed.
project_justification.fill: The project combines an unconditional arm-tape reduction, deterministic two-cohort prefixes, an observable variance gate with a concentration fallback, and same-policy prompt-tilt and hidden-sign experiments. It proves the class-minimax frontier, the ordinary-Wald boundary, the attained bounded-shift calibration, and a conditional prospective follow-up elbow; its Liberali et al. component is an assumption-and-estimand audit rather than asserted trial coverage.

prose_updates.related_work: Shi, Wang, and Wu \cite{ShiWangWu2023DelayedInference} assume independent and identically distributed potential-outcome vectors independent of contemporaneous action and delay, stationary arm-specific delay laws, finite \(2+\delta\) moments, and adaptive-weight conditions. Their Theorems 4.1--4.3 establish DAIPW consistency, asymptotic normality, and variance consistency; Corollary 4.4 verifies those conditions under a one-sided allocation floor, positive prompt mass, and a polynomial finite-delay tail exponent of at least one half, with a nonzero-margin relaxation in Remark 4.5. They do not prove uniform honesty or minimax expected length. This note instead assumes bounded outcomes, explicit rare- and control-arm floors, a known polynomial envelope for every \(\beta>0\), and no infinite delays, while allowing arbitrary within-arm outcome--delay dependence. Hence neither full class contains the other. Only the design-side floor is imported: the prompt sampling converse lies in their independence submodel, whereas the hidden-sign converse deliberately does not. Zhang, Janson, and Murphy \cite{ZhangJansonMurphy2021MEstimators} develop confidence regions for adaptively weighted M-estimators, but not informative delayed revelation or fixed-horizon minimax length. Howard, Ramdas, McAuliffe, and Sekhon \cite{HowardRamdasMcAuliffeSekhon2021} provide time-uniform nonasymptotic confidence sequences on a different axis; they do not solve informative terminal missingness, and the present note is not anytime-valid. Hadad et al. and Bibaut et al. develop predictable weighting and stabilization for prompt adaptive outcomes; Lancewicki et al. and Tang, Wang, and Zheng study reward-dependent-delay bias and regret; Bai, Hu, and Rosenberger and Ma, Wang, and Wei analyze delayed response-adaptive asymptotics under different delay and overlap conditions; Armstrong and Kolesar provide the bounded-bias Gaussian calibration adapted here. Liberali et al. \cite{LiberaliEtAl2025RTAR} report retrospective GUSTO-1 and EUROPA resampling with replacement under stationarity/exchangeability, \(200\) replicates, and empirical \(2.5\%\) and \(97.5\%\) quantiles. Their three-arm GUSTO-1 and two-arm EUROPA examples use daily Gittins allocation and an eta-variant whose equal-randomization component ends at fixed arm minima. Those percentile intervals are neither this note's ordinary-Wald interval nor its hybrid, and their paper certifies neither permanent polynomial/control floors nor a polynomial delay envelope. The reported EUROPA \(4.2\)-year mean time to the last observation is not a tail certificate, so no numerical pad is inferred.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The rate-order frontier, uniform gate theorem, and attained bounded-shift calibration are proved, but exact normalized expected-length constants and the globally optimal variable-length or randomized interval remain open. The construction discards assignments beyond deterministic quotas and is not claimed constant-efficient for policies that explore more aggressively. Uniform validity uses a known tail envelope, independent and identically distributed stationary arrival vectors, bounded outcomes, finite delays implied by that envelope, a control-arm floor, and a prespecified terminal time. Unknown envelope parameters, cross-arrival dependence, nonstationary endpoint rates, odds-ratio targets, and multi-arm protocol transfer are outside scope. The result is fixed-horizon rather than anytime-valid. Liberali et al.'s reported empirical intervals and allocation rules do not satisfy the note's assumptions by citation alone, and their EUROPA follow-up summary cannot determine a numerical pad.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The exact minimax order is over the one-sided forced-exploration class with a control-arm floor. The same fixed policy \(\pi_t(1)=ct^{-\alpha}\) supplies both lower-bound pairs. The sampling converse is compatible with Shi--Wang--Wu outcome--delay independence, but the informative hidden-sign converse is deliberately outside that submodel. On nonempty regular-variance sequences, ordinary Wald is uniformly honest exactly when \(T^q(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}\to0\), with \(q=(1-\alpha)/2\); this yields the stated three-regime prospective follow-up elbow. The Liberali et al. result here is only a source audit: their published intervals are retrospective empirical replicate percentiles, not this note's intervals; their allocation description and EUROPA follow-up summary do not certify the required floors or tail envelope. Conditional on complete ascertainment and the single-reveal encoding, 30 days after final GUSTO-1 randomization removes its 30-day endpoint's delay bias, but does not prove adaptive-Wald validity. A prospective Liberali-style transfer requires a two-arm risk-difference target, permanent logged floors, this note's interval, and a certified tail envelope; odds-ratio and three-arm transfers remain outside scope.
